mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation shock.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the GDP decline is accompanied by a simultaneous surge in industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation exceeds 5% concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month acceleration in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) above 0.5% monthly indicates a supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate revenue prospects and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the acceleration is accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand proxies.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 3% within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based deterioration in demand fundamentals, which reduces earnings growth and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the decline is offset by a surge in industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months during a period of stable inflation signals a labor-market slack regime, which supports accommodative monetary policy and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% for 2 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL change < 0.2% monthly
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or inflation accelerates above 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above 0.8% for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, regardless of the monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the retail sales growth is accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production and consumer confidence.
